records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:47-49 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger disconnected from f, so assertions on FromContext-based logging never record calls, producing silently-passing tests (P3)
records.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/fake.go, the newly added method `func (f *TestLogger) FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger { return NewTestLogger() }` always returns a *new* TestLogger instance, not one linked to `f`. Any code that logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (as added in logger_middleware.go) will record calls on the fresh logger, so assertions against the original `f`'s `InfoLogs/WarnLogs/...` will not observe those calls. This is a concrete behavioral mismatch with how a contextual logger wrapper is expected to work and can mask logging behavior in tests.
records.stripped_text: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go:47-49 — TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger disconnected from f, so assertions on FromContext-based logging never record calls, producing silently-passing tests (P3)

records.issue_text: pkg/plugins/log/logger.go:47-53 — grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext falls back to d.New() when type-assert to *log.ConcreteLogger fails, discarding all contextual attributes set by ContextualLoggerMiddleware (P3)
records.rationale: In pkg/plugins/log/logger.go, grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext(ctx) does `concreteInfraLogger, ok := d.l.FromContext(ctx).(*log.ConcreteLogger)` and if `!ok` returns `d.New()` (no ctx passed). That fallback path necessarily drops any context-derived attributes (e.g., those added via `log.WithContextualAttributes(ctx, p)` in the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware) because it creates a fresh logger not derived from `ctx`.
